summary: MHT-CET engineering college predictor web app; initial frontend form UI exists and focus is now shifting to making the system functional by adding backend predictor logic using dummy data (percentile -> estimated rank -> sample Safe/Probable/Dream results).
architectural_notes: Use SQLite initially for structured storage of cutoff data extracted from CAP PDFs.
Cutoff records stored with fields: year, round, college_name, branch_name, seat_type, category, gender, closing_rank, percentile.
Parse combined cutoff codes (e.g., GOPENH) into gender/category/seat_type attributes.
Prediction compares user estimated rank vs Round 4 closing ranks using thresholds: ≤0.8×cutoff Safe, ≤cutoff Probable, ≤1.2×cutoff Dream.
Frontend-first milestone: build UI without backend/logic initially.
Add a minimal predictor function that maps percentile -> estimated rank using a simple placeholder heuristic (until real data/rank model is implemented).
Expose a lightweight backend endpoint (or server function) that returns dummy results in the format: College | Branch | Chance, to make the form submission functional end-to-end.

existing_features.title: Create a mobile-friendly frontend page that renders a simple MHT-CET college predictor form with these fields and labels: CET Percentile (number input), Category (dropdown: OPEN, OBC, SC, ST, EWS), Gender (dropdown: Male, Female), Candidature (dropdown: Maharashtra, All India), Home University (dropdown containing major Maharashtra universities), TFWS (yes/no), and a Submit button.

Implement basic client-side form state wiring purely for UI purposes (no predictor logic and no backend calls): inputs should be editable, selections should persist in the UI, and submitting should prevent full page reload.

Apply a coherent visual theme across the form (colors, typography, spacing, and components) that feels like an education/exam utility and is consistently used throughout the page; avoid blue/purple as the primary palette.

Wire the existing `frontend/src/pages/MhtCetPredictorFormPage.tsx` submit action to call the backend predictor method using the existing `useActor` hook, and render the returned results in the UI after submission.

Ensure the frontend can call the new backend method by updating the generated frontend backend bindings/types (the `backendInterface` used by `frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts`) to include the predictor method signature and response types.

new_feature_requests.summary: Build a simple mobile-friendly frontend form UI for MHT-CET college predictor (percentile, category, gender, candidature, home university, TFWS) with submit button; no backend/logic yet
Ingest/upload CAP Round 1–4 cutoff PDFs (Maharashtra + All India seats) and extract cutoff tables into structured data
Create SQLite database schema/table for cutoffs (year, round, college, branch, seat_type, category, gender, closing_rank, percentile) including parsing codes like GOPENH
Implement predictor logic: percentile->estimated rank, filter relevant cutoffs, compare to Round 4 closing ranks, classify Safe/Probable/Dream with thresholds
Create results page/table showing college, branch, cutoff percentile, and chance with color coding (Safe green, Probable orange, Dream red)
Prepare the app for deployment as a simple web app

Add simple backend predictor logic for the existing form: convert percentile to estimated rank (placeholder), return dummy/sample college+branch+chance results, and wire it to the UI so submission shows results

Implement a backend predictor method in `backend/main.mo` that accepts the user’s percentile input, converts it to an estimated rank, and returns dummy/sample prediction results with fields `college`, `branch`, and `chance` (values like Dream/Probable/Safe).

projectName: Mobile-friendly MHT-CET college predictor form UI (frontend only)
